critique.good: Dish names remain on one line, making the menu easy to scan. Descriptions form consistent two-line blocks, prices align clearly, and the course bands separate the groups.
critique.problems: The dessert allergen list takes three lines and makes that row taller than the others. The final allergen is split across lines, weakening its association as a phrase.
critique.cause: The 136px Allergens column leaves only 115px for text. The 185px Dish column preserves every name on one line but leaves less space for allergens.

critique.good: The wider allergen column keeps the dessert list to two lines, and prices and course headings remain easy to find.
critique.problems: Most dish names wrap, while two descriptions run to three lines with short final lines. The resulting row heights and text blocks feel uneven, and the allergen column has substantial unused space in several rows.
critique.cause: The 150px Dish and 310px Description columns are narrow for their content; the 201px Allergens column takes space from both.

critique.good: The generous description column keeps every description to two lines, and the course bands and prices remain clear.
critique.problems: Every dish name wraps, with two names taking three lines. This makes the primary scan path fragmented and creates extra row height despite the shorter descriptions. The dessert allergen list also takes three lines.
critique.cause: The 120px Dish column leaves only 99px for names, while the 400px Description column receives more width than needed to keep descriptions to two lines. The 141px Allergens column remains too narrow for the dessert list to fit in two.

critique.good: Course headings are distinct, prices form an easy-to-scan column, and descriptions generally read comfortably in two lines. Words remain intact.
critique.problems: Both main-course names wrap, while the croquettes description ends with a lone “aioli.” The dessert allergen list takes three lines, leaving its final qualifier isolated.
critique.cause: The 175px dish column is still too narrow for the longest names; the 320px description column falls just short of fitting the croquettes description in two lines. The 166px allergen column makes the dessert list wrap to three lines.

critique.good: The 335px description column brings the croquettes description into two balanced lines, producing consistent two-line rows through the starters and mains. Course hierarchy and price scanning remain clear.
critique.problems: Both main-course names wrap, and the dessert allergen list ends with “(hazelnut)” on a third line. The dessert row is consequently taller than the other dish rows.
critique.cause: The 165px dish column cannot hold the longest names on one line. The 161px allergen column is too narrow to fit the dessert list in two lines.

critique.good: The wider allergen column fits the dessert list into two lines and keeps its nut qualifier with the preceding item. Prices and course headings remain easy to find.
critique.problems: The croquettes description ends with a lone “aioli,” and the chicken description ends with a lone “jus.” These three-line descriptions make two rows noticeably taller; both main-course names also wrap.
critique.cause: The 310px description column is too narrow for those descriptions to fit in two lines. The 165px dish column is too narrow for the longest names.

critique.good: Course bands are distinct, prices align for quick comparison, and descriptions read comfortably in two lines. Three dish names remain on one line, and all words stay intact.
critique.problems: Both main-course names wrap, weakening the scan down the dish column. The dessert allergen list takes three lines and determines that row’s height.
critique.cause: The 165px dish column is too narrow for the longest names; the 171px allergen column cannot fit the dessert list in two lines.

critique.good: The wide description column keeps descriptions to two lines, prices and headers stay intact, and course groups are clear.
critique.problems: Four of five dish names wrap, making the identifying column harder to scan without improving the overall row rhythm over r2A. The dessert allergen list still occupies three lines.
critique.cause: Reducing the dish column to 155px gains 10px for descriptions but crosses wrapping thresholds for two additional names; allergens remain at 171px.

critique.good: All dish names fit on one line, making the menu easy to scan by course. Prices and headers remain intact.
critique.problems: The croquettes description ends with a short third line, making that row noticeably taller. The dessert allergens also occupy three lines.
critique.cause: The 185px dish column leaves only 320px for descriptions and 156px for allergens; the description width falls below a useful wrapping threshold for the croquettes.

understanding.purpose: Help diners choose dishes by comparing their descriptions, prices and allergens within each course.
understanding.reading: Readers scan course headings and dish names first, then read across a row for details; the course headings span the full table and should remain distinct from dish rows.
groups: Dish and Description belong together as the name and explanation of each menu item.
Price and Allergens are compact decision aids that readers compare across dishes.
keep_intact: Price values and the Price header
Individual words in dish names, descriptions and allergen lists
The association between each dish and its price and allergens
may_wrap: Descriptions can wrap naturally at word spaces.
Multiword dish names can wrap when needed.
Allergen lists can wrap at natural breaks; description wrapping may already provide enough row height to accommodate them.

bad.why: The narrow dish column would wrap most names across multiple lines and could split a long word, making the row identifiers harder to scan. The extra description width would come at the expense of both dish names and allergen information.

contrast.why: The narrow dish column would wrap most names across multiple lines and could split a long word, making the row identifiers harder to scan. The extra description width would come at the expense of both dish names and allergen information.

final.rationale: In r3A, all five dish names remain on one line, giving the menu a strong scanning edge. The descriptions each fit in two lines, while the price column stays compact and the allergen lists remain readable without breaking words. The dessert allergen list takes three lines, but its extra height keeps the full information together within the row.

general: Give row identifiers enough space to support quick scanning, while reserving width for columns with longer prose.
Judge wrapping across the whole row: a line break matters more when it obscures a label or separates information readers need to read together.
Compact numeric columns can leave more room for text, provided their headers and values fit.
specific: A 185px dish column keeps every dish name on one line in r3A.
At 325px, the descriptions in r3A each fit in two lines; its 151px allergen column requires three lines for the dessert.

final.tradeoffs: A wider allergen column, as in r2A and r3C, gives those lists more room but leaves two main-course names wrapped. A wider dish column makes the names easier to scan, while leaving less room for allergen text.
final.uncertain: The ranges are conservative: only the preferred widths are asserted to be equally good because intermediate widths were not rendered. A designer who gives allergen scanning more weight could reasonably prefer r2A or r3C.

A.why: The columns are well proportioned and the allergen lists are readable, though two descriptions run to three lines and the main dish names wrap.

B.why: The price column takes as much space as the description, leaving long descriptions cramped into four lines and creating large empty areas.

C.why: Descriptions and allergens fit comfortably in two lines, but every dish name wraps, making the row labels harder to scan.

D.why: Descriptions have ample room, but the narrow dish column breaks several names across three lines and the dessert allergens also wrap heavily.

E.why: Descriptions read cleanly in two lines and most dish names stay on one line; the longer main names wrap and the dessert allergen list takes three lines.

F.why: All dish names remain on one line, descriptions are consistently two lines, and the compact price column leaves useful space for the other content. The longest allergen list wraps to three lines but remains readable.

reviews.unsure: E gives allergens slightly more room, but both E and F need three lines for the longest allergen list; F keeps all dish names intact.

A.why: Descriptions mostly fit in two lines, and the narrow price column leaves useful room elsewhere. Two dish names wrap, and the dessert allergens extend to three lines.

B.why: Every dish name stays on one line, descriptions fit comfortably in two, and prices remain easy to scan. The dessert allergen list takes three lines, but the overall proportions are strong.

C.why: Equal column widths give prices far more room than they need while squeezing descriptions into four-line blocks. The resulting tall rows contain large empty areas and make comparisons slower.

D.why: Descriptions and allergen lists fit neatly in two lines, with little wasted space around prices. Every dish name wraps, making the row identifiers less immediate to scan.

E.why: The wide description column keeps prose open, but the dish column breaks several names across three lines. The narrow allergen column also produces a fragmented dessert list.

F.why: The price column is compact and the allergen lists are reasonably open. Some dish names wrap, and two descriptions end with a short third line, creating uneven row rhythm.

reviews.unsure: The choice between B and D depends partly on whether keeping dish names on one line matters more than reducing wrapping in the allergen lists.
